verdict.rationale: Radar Sessions let a developer pass device and behavioral fraud data into Radar even when not tokenizing on Stripe. Custom rules and value lists let business-specific attributes shape outcomes. However, nothing shows a developer feeding their own fingerprints or custom metadata into the ML risk score itself, and the rules sit on top of network scoring rather than retraining it. missing for 10: documented ingestion of merchant-supplied device fingerprints or behavioral signals into the model score, custom metadata as model features, rule attributes referencing custom metadata, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can feed the model my own signals — device fingerprints, behavioral data, custom metadata — so scoring reflects my business, not just network defaults

citations.quote: By using Radar Sessions, you can capture critical fraud information without tokenizing on Stripe.
you can also set up rules that are unique to your business using the supported attributes
Value lists allow you to group values together which can then be referenced in rules.
